entries.full_claim: Any pilot-measurable deterministic selection from a frozen finite menu preserves R164 simultaneous coverage when every menu plan has the conditional planwise guarantee and uses constant confirmatory bets for the same unweighted target.
entries.domain: One fixed R161/R164 protocol, disjoint pilot and confirmatory samples, finite frozen menu, every planwise-valid menu element, and no confirmatory-outcome selection.
all_premises: the menu and deterministic tie-break are frozen before pilot outcomes
every menu element satisfies all R164 coverage premises
confirmatory outcomes are not used for plan, target or report selection
entries.proof_or_source: Pilot_Menu_Width_Certification_and_Feasibility_v0_1.md §3; conditional expectation/tower argument specialized from R162-P2.
entries.counterexample_or_limit: Selecting from confirmatory outcomes can inflate error; finiteness alone does not validate an invalid menu element.
entries.thought_experiment_role: Copy/swap separates design selection from the fixed experience token.

entries.full_claim: Pilot/confirmatory independence alone does not identify or bound confirmatory residual risks or preserve the ranking of predictor centers.
entries.domain: One bounded component, two constant centers and independent deterministic pilot/confirmatory samples.
all_premises: the common constant bet and target are unchanged
entries.counterexample_or_limit: Does not challenge coverage; it challenges only width transport and pilot ranking.
entries.thought_experiment_role: Abacus/calculator devices expose distribution shift despite data-split independence.

entries.full_claim: Under independent bounded pilot participants and declared pilot-to-confirmatory residual-risk radii, the Hoeffding union band covers all m|Q| confirmatory residual risks with probability at least 1-beta; minimizing its upper width certificate has the displayed menu-relative regret bound.
entries.domain: Finite m and Q, finite independent pilot participant vectors, bounded squared residuals, fixed N_q/lambda/c plans, and valid transport radii.
all_premises: the complete finite menu is fixed before pilot outcomes
every declared transport inequality is true
the planning objective is maximum component expected untruncated half-width
entries.proof_or_source: Pilot_Menu_Width_Certification_and_Feasibility_v0_1.md §§5–6; Hoeffding union bound, monotonicity and deterministic upper-certificate minimization.
entries.counterexample_or_limit: No transport premise means no width guarantee; the bound is not a realized-width or power theorem and can be loose.
entries.thought_experiment_role: Human-realized-agent and copy/swap cases isolate independence, transport and selection.

entries.full_claim: The simultaneous lower/upper width certificates justify certified-feasible when min H_U<=w_max, menu-relative design-not-feasible when min H_L>w_max, and pilot-inconclusive otherwise; an upper bound above threshold alone never proves infeasibility.
entries.domain: The exact R165-P3 event, nonempty deterministically admissible menu, fixed threshold and fixed status boundaries.
all_premises: protocol gates and hard resource screen are evaluated first
no status is reinterpreted as a substantive UCT or experiential result
entries.counterexample_or_limit: The decision is relative to menu, objective, transport model, resource cap and beta; equality at the lower boundary remains inconclusive unless an upper certificate passes.
entries.thought_experiment_role: Ancestor and copy/swap cases prevent a design status from becoming an experience predicate.
